textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · Cell: The Building Block of Life · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. Most cells are too small to see, so we study them with microscopes.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. Most cells are too small to see, so we study them with microscopes.
beats.speakEn: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. Most cells are too small to see, so we study them with microscopes.

beats.en: The human eye cannot separate two points closer than about 0.1 mm, so most plant and animal cells, which are much smaller, need a microscope.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · Cell: The Building Block of Life · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: The cell membrane is made of proteins and lipids. It controls what enters and leaves, and its mosaic-like arrangement of molecules is why it is called the fluid mosaic model.

beats.en: The cell membrane is made of proteins and lipids. It controls what enters and leaves, and its mosaic-like arrangement of molecules is why it is called the fluid mosaic model.
beats.speakEn: The cell membrane is made of proteins and lipids. It controls what enters and leaves, and its mosaic-like arrangement of molecules is why it is called the fluid mosaic model.

beats.en: Cells with no true nucleus are called prokaryotic cells. Their genetic material lies in a region called the nucleoid, while eukaryotic cells have a nucleus.
beats.speakEn: Cells with no true nucleus are called prokaryotic cells. Their genetic material lies in a region called the nucleoid, while eukaryotic cells have a nucleus.
